newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Mothers Day boom at Dutch Aalsmeer flower auction.
newsitem.headline: Mothers Day boom at Dutch Aalsmeer flower auction.

text.p: Mothers Day in Britain led to an extra 40 million Dutch guilders worth of business going through the Dutch flower auctions in Aalsmeer an auction spokesman said.

In the first few weeks of March, more than 180 million cut flowers and plants passed through Aalsmeer for British Mothering Sunday on March 9. Of this 168 million pieces were cut flowers, 13 million were house plants and 260,000 were garden plants.

This represented 140 million guilders worth of business to the auction, with the cut flowers being worth 103 million guilders, house plants 34 million and garden plants totalling 1.33 million guilders.

An average week at the Aalsmeer Flower Auction with its seven separate auction halls, would see around 99.5 million guilders worth of business pass through the auctions: 73 million guilders of cut flowers, 25 million guilders of house plants and 470,000 guilders worth of garden plants.

A spokesman for the Aalsmeer Flower Auction said that this year Mothering Day turnover in Britain was stable compared to other years. The majority of the cut flowers were roses and some tulips, he added, with many of these being produced in the Netherlands.
Although, at the same time, many flowers and plants are airfreighted in from countries such as Israel, Kenya, Colombia, Nairobi, Zimbabwe, Equador and Costa Rica.
However, it appears the Dutch are a little more enthusiastic for Mothers Day - especially for garden plants.

Last year, the Dutch bought 160 million guilders worth of flowers and plants during the Mothers Day period in May. The Dutch were nearly as keen on cut flowers as the British, buying 100 million guilders worth of cut flowers. Aalsmeer is expecting this coming Mothers Day in the Netherlands to be just as busy, said the spokesman adding that over the last three years Valentine's Day has also become much more important in the Netherlands. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
